title: Vesper and the Songbook
premise: Ansel Ishikawa, a once-celebrated cellist whose hands froze mid-concert, hides out in a fading mountain town repairing violins and avoiding music entirely. When a snowstorm traps him with Vesper Quill, the rival who beat him for the conservatory's final solo a decade ago and now runs the bakery downstairs, old resentments thaw into something neither planned. As the bakery lease expires and a developer circles the block, Ansel must choose between staying invisible and testifying about the conservatory's cover-up of his breakdown, a truth that could save the building but expose them both. In the end, Ansel plays publicly for the first time since the collapse, Vessel's bakery is saved by the town they've quietly become family with, and the two rivals sign the lease together.
about_author: Rosalind Villalobos is a former music teacher from northern New Mexico who writes love stories about people rebuilding after public failure. She lives with her partner, two opinionated cats, and a piano she refuses to tune.

chapters.title: The Silence After
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Three years after his catastrophic final performance, Ansel repairs violins in a drafty apartment above Vesper's bakery, flinching at every note. A tuning fork in his drawer he never uses establishes his wound. Beat: isolation as armor.

chapters.title: Flour and Ash
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper Quill, the rival who won the solo Ansel lost, runs her bakery on a knife's edge of debt, hiding her own failed career behind croissants. She recognizes Ansel's name on a repair ticket and says nothing. Beat: two people performing normalcy.

chapters.title: The Storm Door
chapters.summary: Alternating. An early blizzard knocks out power; Ansel descends to warn Vesper and they're trapped together by a fallen tree across the road. Forced proximity, awkward history, shared whiskey. Beat: the past knocks, uninvited.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Bad Timing
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Over candlelight, the rivalry surfaces: the conservatory solo, the rumors, the night Ansel's hands failed. Each believed the other sabotaged them. First real argument. Beat: resentment revealed as mutual grief.

chapters.title: What the Hands Remember
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel admits the breakdown wasn't nerves but a neurological injury the conservatory pressured him to hide. Vesper realizes her 'victory' was handed to a man being quietly destroyed. Beat: the mistake they both made was believing the institution.

chapters.title: Bread at Midnight
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper teaches Ansel to knead dough, the first rhythmic work his hands tolerate. Small joy, first laugh. Neighbor Marisol's kid wanders in, the found-family seed planted. Beat: tenderness as risk.

chapters.title: The Letter from Halloway
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A letter arrives: the conservatory's former dean, Halloway, is being honored, and a journalist is investigating the era's cover-ups. Ansel's testimony could matter. Panic; he nearly burns the letter. Beat: the past demands a price.

chapters.title: Lease Terms
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The developer's offer arrives: sell the building or face eviction in sixty days. Vesper hides it from Ansel, repeating her old pattern of going it alone. Beat: pride as self-sabotage.

chapters.title: Duet, Unwilling
chapters.summary: Alternating. To raise money, Vesper proposes a winter concert series in the bakery; Ansel refuses to play but agrees to organize. They work side by side, friction becoming rhythm. Beat: collaboration as courtship.

chapters.title: The Town That Stayed
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Marisol, the hardware store owner, the retired choir teacher all sign on to help. Ansel, who kept everyone at arm's length, is startled to be known. Beat: found family arrives without permission.

chapters.title: First Frost, First Kiss
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. After a successful first concert Ansel attends but doesn't play, they kiss in the flour-dusted kitchen. Vesper immediately pulls back, terrified of ruining the one thing working. Beat: joy shadowed by fear.

chapters.title: The Journalist
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The journalist, Dana, finds Ansel and lays out evidence: Halloway knew Ansel's injury was work-preventable and buried the medical report. Testimony could win a settlement, enough to save the building. Beat: justice dangles, costly.

chapters.title: What Vesper Knew
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Ansel discovers Vesper knew about Dana's investigation weeks ago and stayed silent, fearing he'd leave. The rivalry's old wound reopens: they protect themselves before each other. Beat: the real obstacle is trust, not love.

chapters.title: Sixty Days
chapters.summary: Alternating. Cold war in a shared kitchen; the concert series continues out of stubbornness, not warmth. Marisol forces them to co-chair the finale. Beat: grief needs a middle passage.

chapters.title: The Mirror in the Practice Room
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel secretly tries to play again; his hands fail and he shatters a borrowed cello. Vesper finds him among the wreckage and stays. Beat: the person in the mirror is the one who most needs forgiving.

chapters.title: Confession in Proofing Dough
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper confesses her own secret: she withdrew from the solo tour years later out of terror, not triumph, and has been failing ever since. Two failures, finally face to face. Beat: mutual absolution begins.

chapters.title: Halloway's Honor
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel attends the dean's gala unannounced and hears Halloway accept praise for 'protecting young musicians.' Something in him settles: he will testify. Beat: resolve crystallizes.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel gives his statement to Dana and the conservatory's oversight board, naming names, with Vesper's hand in his outside the door. Beat: justice outside the law's comfort—truth as the only available verdict.

chapters.title: The Finale
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. The bakery's final concert. Ansel walks on stage, hands shaking, and plays a short, imperfect piece—his first public performance since the collapse. The room holds him. Beat: climax; second chances taken, not given.

chapters.title: Verdicts and Vouchers
chapters.summary: Alternating. The conservatory settles quietly; the settlement and town donations cover the lease buyout. Ansel and Vesper, still raw, must decide what they are now that the crisis is over. Beat: love without adrenaline.

chapters.title: Signing the Lease
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper rewrites the lease with two names. Ansel opens a small teaching studio upstairs; Marisol's kid is his first student. The town gathers for the signing. Beat: found family formalized.

chapters.title: Vesper, at Last
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A year later: bread at dawn, students at noon, a duet in the kitchen at night. Ansel reflects that timing was never the enemy—hiding was. Final image: the tuning fork, finally rung. Beat: home, earned.
